newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X chief awaits word from Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X chief awaits word from Indonesia.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Thursday that he does not know when the Indonesian government will approve Bre-X's proposed deal with Barrick Gold Corp to develop Indonesia's huge Busang gold deposit.
"We are waiting for the government to get back to us," David Walsh said in an interview from Calgary.
Walsh said he had read an Indonesian news report that suggested the Minister of Mines would respond to the two companies next week, but he said he had no confirmation of the report.

Bre-X and Barrick said earlier this week they had reached a joint proposed deal to develop Busang. The companies presented the proposal to the Indonesian government, and said they would not announce the terms of the deal until they heard back from the government.
"As soon as we have ministerial approval and answers to certain questions put to (the government), we'll be able to announce the terms and conditions," Walsh said.
He said he should be able to discuss the terms before the Indonesian government grants contracts of work for Busang.

The Indonesian government told Bre-X in November to form a joint venture with Barrick, with Barrick getting 75 percent, Bre-X keeping 25 percent and the two companies arranging for the government to get a 10 percent cut.
While Bre-X shareholders have cried out about being forced into Barrick's arms, Walsh said they will not be disappointed with the terms of the deal.
"As a result of our negotiating team, we were able substantially enhance the Barrick offer," he said. "I think the shareholders will be pleased with the job we've done."
He said Bre-X had received two previous offers that were not as attractive as the Barrick offer.
Earlier this week Walsh said both Bre-X and Barrick had some concerns about their arrangement and had asked the government for clarification.
